title: Meet the chapter. [[Know how to take part.]]
hook: A one-page website concept for BNI Victory, a business-networking chapter in Goa. The page moves from what the chapter is for, to who is in it, to how to ask for an invitation.

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Information hierarchy and website visual design

facts.label: Why
facts.value: A brief I set myself: a website for a local business-networking chapter

facts.label: Platform
facts.value: Desktop web page, designed 1920 px wide

facts.label: Scope
facts.value: One long page: invitation, purpose, people and contact. Sample content in the people cards

facts.label: Status
facts.value: Design concept. Not built, tested or launched

summary: The problem: a business owner hearing about a networking chapter wants to know what it is for, who is in it, and how to take a first step.
What I did: I designed one long page with an invitation at the top, the chapter's purpose, two kinds of people cards and a contact form.
The key idea: let people carry the page. Leaders and members take up 46% of its length.
Where it stands: a 2023 concept with no research behind it. The people cards hold sample content, and the worldwide BNI numbers in the About text are not results of this project.

lead.alt: The whole BNI Victory page shown in four columns: hero and About, mission and leaders, leaders and members, contact form and footer
lead.caption: The whole page, read left to right in four columns. Faces, names and contact details are blurred or covered, here and in every picture below.

sections.label: The brief
sections.heading: I set myself a brief: make a first visit feel possible

blocks.p: This was a brief I set myself. I did no interviews and no testing, so this page is about the design and nothing else.

I pictured a business owner who has just heard of the chapter. I assumed they would ask three things, in this order, and I put the page in the same order. The questions are my assumption, not a research finding.

figures.alt: Diagram pairing three visitor questions with the sections of the page that answer them
figures.caption: Three questions and the sections that answer them: purpose first, then people, then the invitation.

aside.title: Two limits to be clear about.
aside.detail: The About text quotes BNI's own worldwide numbers. They describe the organisation, not anything this project achieved. The people cards repeat the same sample person twelve times, so they show a layout and not a real chapter's members.

sections.label: Page structure
sections.heading: One page in nine bands, and nearly half of it is people

blocks.p: The concept is a single page, 1920 px wide and 9919 px tall. The four links in the navigation match its main parts. The two people sections are the largest. Together they fill 46% of the page, more than purpose and contact combined.

figures.alt: Scaled picture of the full page beside a list of its nine bands and the share of the page each one takes
figures.caption: The page from top to bottom, drawn to scale. Compare Our Leaders at 28% with the hero at 8%.

sections.label: The first screen
sections.heading: The first screen makes one offer: get invited

blocks.p: The hero, the large opening area of a page, has one button. It says Get Invited, not Join. An invitation to visit is a smaller step than signing up, so it is an easier first thing to ask for.

figures.alt: The navigation, hero and contact strip with seven numbered markers and a note for each
figures.caption: The first screen with its seven parts marked. Look at 4: it is the only button, so there is no doubt about what to press.

blocks.p: The trade-off is that the button promises something the concept does not show. The next screen would have to explain what a visit involves and who can come.
Two sections explain what the chapter is for. About Us sets a paragraph beside a mosaic of portraits. Our Mission is a single card, half photo and half red, with the mission in large white type.

figures.alt: The About Us section: a red ribbon heading, a justified paragraph on the left and a blurred mosaic of portrait photos on the right
figures.caption: About Us. The mosaic fades into red towards the right edge. The numbers in the paragraph are BNI's worldwide figures, not results of this project.

figures.alt: The Our Mission card: a photo of a speaker at a lectern on the left blending into a red panel with the mission text on the right
figures.caption: Our Mission. The photo blends into the red panel with no hard edge between them.

blocks.p: Every section opens with the same red ribbon, set on a background made of the logo repeated in very pale grey. Someone scrolling quickly can still see where each section starts.

figures.alt: A red ribbon with the words About Us at the left edge of the page, over a pale pattern of repeated BNI logos
figures.caption: The ribbon and the logo pattern behind it. The same pair marks About Us, Our Leaders, Team Members and Contact Us.

sections.label: People
sections.heading: Two kinds of card for two kinds of member

blocks.p: Leaders and members get different cards. A leader card is tall and has room for a short biography. A member card is compact and swaps the biography for two buttons, one for email and one for phone. I have redrawn both here without the photos or sample details.

figures.alt: Two redrawn cards side by side with numbered notes: a tall leader card with a biography and a shorter member card with email and phone buttons
figures.caption: The two card types, redrawn. Compare item 3 on each: leaders are introduced, members can be contacted.

figures.alt: The Our Leaders ribbon above a row of three tall white cards, with portraits and text blurred
figures.caption: One row of leader cards from the mock-up, with the sample content blurred.

figures.alt: The Team Members ribbon above a row of three shorter grey cards with a curved red lower edge, with portraits and text blurred
figures.caption: One row of member cards. The curved red edge holds the social icons.

blocks.p: The trade-off is upkeep. A directory like this needs each member's permission, checked biographies and someone to keep it up to date. Repeated sample content, as in my mock-up, would weaken a real page.

sections.label: Type and colour
sections.heading: One main typeface and one red

blocks.p: I measured the type on the page. Nearly all of it is one round sans in a few weights. Sizes run from 82.5 px for the contact heading down to 25 px for links, with a few smaller labels.

figures.alt: Eight samples of text cut from the page, each with its measured size and where it is used
figures.caption: Real samples from the page, all at the same scale. The ribbons, the hero headline and the mission heading are close in size, between 60 and 70 px.

blocks.p: Colour is just as narrow. One red marks ribbons, buttons, the mission card and the rings round portraits. Orange appears in two small places. Everything else is white, grey or near-black.

figures.alt: Six colour swatches with their hex values and where each is used on the page
figures.caption: The six colours on the page. Red is the only strong one.

sections.label: The way in
sections.heading: Three ways to reach the chapter, each one step long

blocks.p: A visitor can reach the chapter from the hero, from the navigation or from the footer. Each route ends at a button or a link. What comes after it was not designed.

figures.alt: Flow diagram of three routes: hero to Get Invited, the Contact Us link to the form, and the footer to three membership links, each ending in a step that was not designed
figures.caption: The three routes. The dashed boxes on the right are where this concept ends.

blocks.p: The contact form is the only route with a second step on the page. It asks for a name, an email and a message.

figures.alt: The Contact Us section with six numbered markers: the ribbon, the logo, the heading, three form fields, the button and three social icons
figures.caption: The contact section. Compare 3 and 5: the heading is the largest text on the page, and the button that sends the form has the smallest text in the section.

blocks.p: The footer repeats the four section links and adds three named for the wider organisation: BNI Global, Become a Member and Find a Chapter.

figures.alt: The dark footer with the chapter logo and a short description, a Website column of seven links and a Contact column with its details covered
figures.caption: The footer. I have covered the contact details in the right-hand column.

sections.label: What comes next
sections.heading: The invitation needs real people and a clear next step

blocks.p: A page about a community is only as believable as the people on it. Before growing the directory I would confirm the chapter's details, its members' permission and how a visit works.

list: Replace the sample cards with real, checked content for each member.
Explain how a visitor meeting works before the Get Invited button, and design the screen that follows it.
Shorten the page with a tighter summary near the top and direct links to meeting details.
Test it. Ask a possible visitor what the chapter does, whether it suits their business, and what they expect to happen after asking for an invitation.

blocks.p: None of this was built or tested, so there are no results to report.
